company.name: Heart Aerospace
company.shortDescription: Heart Aerospace is a Swedish startup making electric regional airplanes.
company.description:
Heart’s mission is to create the fastest, most affordable and sustainable transportation for regional travel to every corner of the world.
Their first aircraft is the ES-19, a nineteen-passenger airliner with an operating range of 400 km. Heart's goal is to have the aircraft certified for commercial operation by 2026.

aiResearchSummary.text: Heart Aerospace is developing a method of managing conditioning fluid of a thermal management system for an aircraft, alongside an aerospace thermal management system for a hybrid electric aircraft that cools electric propulsion units via multiple fluid circuits. They also work on an aerospace electric propulsion thermal management system with coordinated motor and power electronics cooling, an energy distribution system for prioritizing aircraft electrical loads, systems for charging and redistributing power in multi powertrain aircraft, and a modular thermal management system. Together these focus on thermal control, electric propulsion, power distribution, charging and powertrain integration.

insights.implication: This round accounts for most reported historical financing, making it important when assessing funding-source concentration and fundraising cadence.

insights.statement: 2 disclosed grants total $7,014,150, representing 4.64% of reported funding.
insights.implication: The grants reduce the share of reported financing attributed to equity or notes, although their restrictions and milestone requirements need separate verification.

insights.title: Valuation increased across disclosed rounds
insights.statement: Known post-money valuation rose from $2,425,632 to $626,416,658, a 258.25x increase.
insights.implication: The disclosed financing history indicates a material valuation step-up between the earliest and latest rounds with known valuations.
caveats: Only rounds with a disclosed post-money valuation are compared.
